cards.prose: Both gospels give the warning in the same words, but Mark sets it on the Mount of Olives with Peter and James and John and Andrew asking privately what the sign would be. Matthew has the disciples ask about his coming and the end of the world. Either way, the first thing Yahusha (Jesus) says is that deceivers will use his name.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew gives the same warning as the answer to the disciples' question about the sign of his coming and of the end of the world.

cards.prose: Luke carries the same warning and adds two things Mark does not: the deceivers will say *the time draweth near*, and Yahusha (Jesus) gives the plain order *go ye not therefore after them*. He does not only say such men will come; he tells his hearers not to follow.
cards.member_sentence: Luke adds that the deceivers will say the time is near, and Yahusha (Jesus) tells his hearers not to go after them.

cards.prose: Paul found the same danger at Corinth: a man comes preaching *another Yahusha (Jesus)*, bringing another spirit and another gospel, and the people are ready to put up with him. What Yahusha (Jesus) said would come in his name was already walking into a congregation.
cards.member_phrase: preacheth another Yahusha (Jesus), whom we have not preached, or if ye receive another spirit
cards.member_sentence: Paul warns that someone may preach another Yahusha (Jesus), another spirit and another gospel than the one the Corinthians first received.

cards.prose: Paul is amazed at how quickly people were *so soon removed* from the one who called them *unto another gospel*. The warning Yahusha (Jesus) gave on the Mount of Olives was not about a far-off day; Paul saw it already happening in the assemblies of Galatia.
cards.member_sentence: Paul marvels that the Galatians have so soon turned from the one who called them to another gospel, which is the very deception Mark warns of.

cards.prose: Moses had said it long before: a prophet may give a sign or a wonder and still not be from Yahuah (the LORD). The very next words show what the test is, *Let us go after other gods, which thou hast not known* (Deuteronomy 13:2). Yahusha (Jesus) is sending his disciples back to that test.
cards.member_sentence: Moses already taught that a prophet's sign or wonder proves nothing by itself, so the warning in Mark sends the hearers back to the test he gave.

cards.prose: John saw a beast that does *great wonders* and brings *fire come down from heaven* in the sight of men. Mark gives the warning beforehand; Revelation shows what such wonders look like when they are staged for everyone to watch.
cards.member_sentence: Revelation shows wonders done openly in the sight of men, with fire called down from heaven, as the kind of sign Mark warns about.

cards.prose: Paul says where such wonders come from: the coming of the one he describes is *after the working of Satan*, with *all power and signs and lying wonders*. That is why Yahusha (Jesus) can say signs and wonders might seduce even the elect. They can be lying wonders, power and all.
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the wicked one comes after the working of Satan with power and signs and lying wonders, which is how the elect could be seduced.

cards.prose: Joel sees the lights go out as the army of Yahuah (the LORD) comes, and he names the time: *the day of Yahuah (LORD) is great and very terrible* (Joel 2:11). When Yahusha (Jesus) says the sun and moon will be darkened, he is pointing at that day of the prophets, not at a new sign.
cards.member_phrase: the sun and the moon shall be dark, and the stars shall withdraw their shining
cards.member_sentence: Joel puts the darkening of the sun, moon and stars at the coming of the day of Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.prose: Isaiah adds the stars and their constellations to the darkened sun and moon, and he sets all of it in a day of judgment: *Behold, the day of Yahuah (LORD) cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger* (Isaiah 13:9). Yahusha (Jesus) says *the moon shall not give her light* and speaks in the same line of the prophet.
cards.member_phrase: the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah says the stars and constellations, the sun and the moon, will give no light on the day of Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.prose: In Isaiah the darkness goes further: the host of heaven *shall be dissolved* and the heavens *rolled together as a scroll*, falling like a leaf from a vine. It comes when *the indignation of Yahuah (LORD) is upon all nations* (Isaiah 34:2), so Yahusha (Jesus) is using a picture of judgment the prophet already drew.
cards.member_phrase: the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah says the host of heaven will be dissolved and the heavens rolled together like a scroll in the day of Yahuah's (the LORD's) judgment.

cards.prose: Daniel saw *one like the Son of Adam* come *with the clouds of heaven* to the Ancient of days, and Daniel's next verse says what was given him: *his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away* (Daniel 7:14). Yahusha (Jesus) says it outright in Mark: the one they will see coming is the one Daniel saw.
cards.member_phrase: behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days
cards.member_sentence: Daniel saw one like the Son of Adam come with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of days, and Mark names him as Yahusha (Jesus).

cards.prose: Matthew has the same coming and adds two things Mark does not: *the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven* appears first, and *all the tribes of the earth mourn* when they see him. Mark says only that they will see him; Matthew tells what the seeing does to the tribes.
cards.member_phrase: then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven
cards.member_sentence: Matthew adds the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven and the mourning of all the tribes of the earth when they see him come.

cards.prose: John sees the same coming: *he cometh with clouds*, and *every eye shall see him*, even *they also which pierced him*. Where Mark says they shall see, Revelation says who is among the seers and that *all kindreds of the earth shall wail* because of him.
cards.member_phrase: every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him
cards.member_sentence: Revelation says he comes with clouds, every eye sees him, those who pierced him included, and the kindreds of the earth wail.

cards.prose: Here the one who speaks says *they shall look upon me whom they have pierced*, and the mourning that follows is for him, like the grief for *his only son*. Mark says they will see the Son of Adam coming; Zechariah says what that seeing is, a looking upon the one who was pierced.
cards.member_phrase: they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son
cards.member_sentence: Zechariah says they will look upon the one they pierced and mourn for him as one mourns an only son or a firstborn.

cards.prose: Matthew has the Son of Adam send his angels too, but on another errand: they *gather out of his kingdom all things that offend*. Mark shows what the angels do for the elect; Matthew shows that the kingdom is cleared of offenders before the elect are brought in.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew has the angels first gather out of the kingdom all things that offend and those who do iniquity.

cards.prose: Ezekiel says who is being gathered and from where: *the children of Yashar'el (Israel)*, taken *from among the heathen, whither they be gone*. The elect Mark has coming from the four winds are these scattered children, and Ezekiel says where they are brought, *their own land*.
cards.member_phrase: I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone
cards.member_sentence: Ezekiel says Yahuah (the LORD) will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen and gather them on every side.

cards.prose: Moses promised that wherever any of the scattered had been driven, even to the outmost parts of heaven, Yahuah (the LORD) himself would gather and fetch them from there. Mark gives the same reach in the mouth of Yahusha (Jesus): the elect come from *the uttermost part of the earth* all the way to *the uttermost part of heaven*.
cards.member_phrase: from thence will Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gather thee, and from thence will he fetch thee
cards.member_sentence: Moses says that those driven out to the outmost parts of heaven will be gathered and fetched from there by Yahuah (the LORD).

new_threads.title: Signs and wonders do not vouch for the prophet
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. Yahusha (Jesus) warns the four who asked him privately on the Mount of Olives that the deceivers will not come empty-handed:

*For false Christs and false prophets shall rise, and shall shew signs and wonders, to seduce, if it were possible, even the elect.* (Mark 13:22)

Moses had already told Yashar'el (Israel) that a sign proves nothing by being a sign. What matters is where the man who gives it is leading:

*If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder,* (Deuteronomy 13:1)

*And the sign or the wonder come to pass, whereof he spake unto thee, saying, Let us go after other gods, which thou hast not known, and let us serve them;* (Deuteronomy 13:2)

The answer Moses gives is the commandments themselves:

*Ye shall walk after Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), and fear him, and keep his commandments, and obey his voice, and ye shall serve him, and cleave unto him.* (Deuteronomy 13:4)

So a wonder that comes to pass is no proof. The test is whether the one who works it keeps the people walking in the commandments or draws them away.

John saw wonders of this kind in Revelation, in his own vision:

*And he doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men,* (Revelation 13:13)

And Paul, writing to the Thessalonians, says where such power comes from:

*Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders,* (2 Thessalonians 2:9)

Moses, John and Paul agree with what Yahusha (Jesus) says in Mark: signs and wonders can be seen, and they can still seduce.

new_threads.title: The Son of Adam coming in the clouds
new_threads.summary_md:
Yahusha (Jesus) answers the four who asked him privately by naming himself as the one Daniel saw:

*And then shall they see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds with great power and glory.* (Mark 13:26)

Daniel saw him in a night vision, and what he saw was one like the Son of Adam:

*I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* (Daniel 7:13)

Daniel goes on to say what was given him:

*And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.* (Daniel 7:14)

Matthew tells the same coming and adds the mourning of the tribes:

*And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30)

John, in Revelation, says every eye will see him:

*Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen.* (Revelation 1:7)

And Zechariah, long before, has the speaker say of the pierced one:

*And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.* (Zechariah 12:10)

The one Daniel saw and the one Mark names are one, and the seeing ends in mourning for the one who was pierced.
